frontier.hypothesis: The final callback block's jalr-delay-slot residual (D_8009BE7C-clear store filled into the D_8009BE80 jalr's delay slot instead of target's explicit pre-jalr store + unfilled nop) may qualify as a fourth catalogued use-site shape under legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched (guard-clear-and-invoke), closing the last 2/187 instructions once ruled on.
frontier.mechanism: policy/ruling question, not a GCC pass
frontier.next_probe: File a ruling-request citing memory/grind/_exeque/rejected/volatile-D_8009BE7C-guard-clear.c, hypotheses.md H6, src/display.c's DMACallback(2, _exeque) IRQ-install site, and that the floor has now been flat at 2/187 for five consecutive sessions (s4-s8) across permuter, structural, enumerate, and synthesis modalities with zero improvement found by any non-volatile lever.

frontier.hypothesis: A non-volatile pure-C lever may still exist by restructuring how D_8009BE7C's ADDRESS is computed (not the callback pointer, which s7 already falsified as a fresh local across 19 combinations) so the store's address pseudo lands in a call_used_reg the D_8009BE80 jalr itself needs live across the jump, excluding the store from reorg.c's delay-slot fill on a genuine resource conflict.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 reorg.c mark_set_resources for CALL_INSN with include_delayed_effects=1 (reorg.c:573-604): marks every call_used_reg ($v0/$v1/$a0-$a3/$t0-$t9) as SET by the call; a delay-slot candidate must not need a resource the call needs (e.g. the callee-address register) to be excluded from the fill.
frontier.next_probe: Read the .sched/.combine dump (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 _exeque) for the exact hard register the D_8009BE80 indirect-call target materializes into, then try C-level spellings of D_8009BE7C's address expression (e.g. field/struct-access instead of &D_8009BE7C, or computing it via a path that shares register pressure with the callback-address load) designed to force the store's address pseudo into that same register class.
